title: Riff bands of the era, Troy Floyd and C.G. Conn instruments
summary: Blue Devils, Basie, Lunceford, Trent and Troy Floyd's Orchestra of Gold; Conn supplied Albert's trumpets.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What bands were famous for their riffs then?

Well, most all bands. All of them set their riffs. The Blue Devils, which was Ben and Morton's band, great riff band. And of course, from there came the Count Basie band. And you had Lansford, my band, Andy Craig, T Holder, Troy Floyd, Trent. Now Trent was a little more sophisticated band, something on the P-Rong style band. Played mostly the high class hotels and schools and colleges in those days. But they also played a lot of gigs, outside gigs. It was one of these real fine, classy bands, Trent was. Troy was also, but not... To me, Trent was a more refined band, if I have to say it myself. The thing about Troy Floyd's band, were the instruments, everyone had beautiful instruments. It was called the Orchestra of Gold. And in those days, I didn't have to buy my instruments. C.G. Khan gave me my instruments and used my picture in the little folders to advertise me playing a C.G. Khan trumpet. I wish I could find some of these old memoirs, but I just can't find them.
I know some of the guys that work for C.G. Khan, and maybe we should ask them.

I believe it's a long shot. You'd have to go way back to where the original office was in those days, which I can't recall. And they possibly might have something on the shelf. It goes way back to 26 and 27.
